summary_paragraph: A man with a history of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, COPD, and cocaine dependence was admitted for shortness of breath following recent crack cocaine use. He presented with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and chest tightness. Evaluation revealed worsening interstitial lung opacities consistent with cocaine-induced pneumonitis and COPD exacerbation, without evidence of infection or volume overload. He was treated with prednisone and nebulizers, leading to gradual improvement in oxygenation and respiratory symptoms. His heart failure was managed with resumption of torsemide and other cardiac medications. Kidney function, initially impaired, improved with hydration. Diabetes was managed with increased insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue steroids, monitor weight, and avoid substance use.
